findings.passage: “The voter ID case involves the ability of all citizens to cast their vote on Election Day.   There is no evidence of voter fraud and obstacles to voting should not be permitted.  The requirement that voters have photo ID before their vote is counted will cause immediate harm for seniors, the poor, students and others.
findings.note: Statement as Senate floor leader on the Supreme Court hearing of the 2012 photo ID law. Quoted from his Voter ID archive page.

findings.passage: “Eligible voters should go and exercise their right to vote on Election Day and not worry about whether they have a photo ID.
findings.note: Statement on the Commonwealth Court order blocking the photo ID law for the November 2012 election.

findings.passage: “Senate Democrats have said clearly and repeatedly that the voter ID law was an overreach that would result in the disenfranchisement of hundreds of thousands of voters.
findings.note: Reaction to the court striking down the 2012 photo ID law.

findings.passage: “The case fell apart almost immediately because the court rightly saw there was no evidence of fraud.
findings.note: Statement on the administration's decision not to appeal the ruling against the photo ID law.
